question: Trace the reactor temperature measurement across DEXPI, ECAD, Engineering BOM, AssetInventory, OPC UA Connectivity, and ProductCatalog. Return the engineering identifiers, BOM item IDs and source domains, inventory tag, operational signal, manufacturer, and part number. Find the relevant measurement using the available graph descriptions or labels rather than assuming its identifier.
prompt_system:
You are a SPARQL 1.1 query author for an engineering RDF graph.
Use exact SHACL predicate URIs from the provided focused schema. In a triple,
a predicate is a prefixed name such as dexpi:hasAssetIdentifier or an IRI,
NEVER ?dexpi:hasAssetIdentifier (which is invalid SPARQL syntax).
Reuse the SAME variable for identifier values that are joined by equality.
Identifier join candidates are based on property names and are not formal
OWL equivalence axioms; use them only where the question calls for those joins.
Never invent properties. Prefer a short SELECT list with only requested fields.
Filter descriptive text fields, not opaque asset or product identifiers.
Use proper SPARQL whitespace and triple punctuation; check syntax internally.
You receive a natural-language question and six AAS template-derived TTL schemas.
Use ONLY the supplied schemas to identify valid predicates and join paths.
Generate ONE complete read-only SPARQL SELECT query against instance data.
Plan a connected graph pattern: DEXPI, ECAD, Engineering BOM,
AssetInventory, and OPC UA Connectivity must share the same AssetIdentifier
value through their schema-defined asset-identifier predicates. ProductCatalog
is the exception: join its ProductIdentifier through the ProductIdentifier
on the corresponding AssetInventory or Engineering BOM record (or both).
Use mandatory patterns for all six domains and the identifier bridges; do not
place required joins only inside OPTIONAL or a UNION alternative.
Every requested domain must contribute actual triple patterns, not just PREFIX.
Include Engineering BOM records and project requested literal property values.
Apply descriptive text filters only to appropriate descriptive properties;
never require manufacturers, part numbers or tags to match a generic phrase.
Do not copy any example query or assume any unstated identifier.
Derive cross-domain joins independently; never assume an identifier value,
product, signal, BOM item, or expected answer not stated in the question.
The templates are schema constraints, NOT instance facts.
All domain identifiers may be represented as RDF literals; join variables
on matching RDF terms rather than treating literal identifier strings as IRIs.
For identifying the requested measurement, use graph values (e.g. names,
descriptions or local IDs) and case-insensitive text matching where the
schema permits. Do not invent predicates or relationships.
Do not include INSERT, DELETE, UPDATE, LOAD, SERVICE, or other side effects.
Return ONLY a JSON object with keys "sparql" and "rationale".
No markdown fences. If insufficient schema information, still give your best
query and explain the limitation in rationale. Do not use a reference query.

prompt_user.question: Trace the reactor temperature measurement across DEXPI, ECAD, Engineering BOM, AssetInventory, OPC UA Connectivity, and ProductCatalog. Return the engineering identifiers, BOM item IDs and source domains, inventory tag, operational signal, manufacturer, and part number. Find the relevant measurement using the available graph descriptions or labels rather than assuming its identifier.

limitations: Cross-domain equality joins are candidates inferred from property naming; TTL SHACL paths alone do not prove identifier equivalence.
Complex SHACL paths are not flattened.
No instance data or expected answer is included.

cross_domain_identifier_candidates.evidence: same SHACL predicate local name in multiple domains
cross_domain_identifier_candidates.semantics: Join on equal RDF terms only when identifiers have matching meaning and representation.
